questions.question: Which of the following is the largest freshwater lake in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wular.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Wular Lake is the largest freshwater lake in India and lies in the Kashmir Valley.
 
• Wular Lake is also one of the largest freshwater lakes in Asia.
 
• It is sited in the Bandipora district in Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The lake basin was formed as a result of tectonic activity and is fed by the Jhelum River.
 
• The lake's size varies seasonally from 12 to 100 square miles.
 
• Wular Lake is important to fish habitat, the main species being the common carp, rosy barb, mosquitofish, Nemacheilus species, etc.

• Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake in North East India and is famous for the phumdis (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil and organic matter at various stages of decomposition) floating over it.
 
• The lake is located at Moirang in Manipur state, India.
 
• Loktak Day is observed every year on the 15th of October at the periphery of the Loktak lake.
 
• This ancient lake plays an important role in the economy of Manipur. It serves as a source of water for hydropower generation, irrigation and drinking water supply.
 
• The lake is also a source of livelihood for the rural fishermen who live in the surrounding areas and on phumdis, also known as phumshongs.

**Bhimtal Lake-**

 
• One of the well-known lake cities in the **Kumaon region (****Uttarakhand****)** is Bhimtal.
 
• In honor of the well-known Mahabharata character Bheem, Bhimtal was formerly called "Bheemsarovar Lake."
 
• According to mythology, the Pandavas used to travel back to Bhimtal during their exile to visit their home.
 
• As a result, the Bhimeshwar Mahadev temple was built here in honor of Bheema.

**Barapani Lake-**

 
• Barapani Lake is situated in ** Meghalaya.**
 
• Barapani Lake is also known as **Umiam**** Lake.**
 
• It is an artificial water reservoir created by damming the **Umiam river.**

questions.question: The largest dam in India, the Hirakud Dam, is built on which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Mahanadi__.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• Hirakud Dam is the longest earthen dam in the world.
 
• It is constructed across the great river Mahanadi.
 
• The bulk of the Hirakud dam contains earth, concrete, and masonry materials.
 
• From horizon to horizon the reservoir forms the largest artificial lake in Asia with an area of 746 sq. Km. and shoreline over 640 Km.
 
• The project was formally inaugurated by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on 13th January 1957.
 
• The installed capacity for power generation is 347.5 MW through its two powerhouses at Burla, at the right bank, and Chiplima, at 22 km downstream of Dam.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** **Godavari:**

 
• The Godavari river is the largest river system in Peninsular India.
 
• The Godavari basin extends over the States of Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha in addition to smaller parts in Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, and Puducherry (Yanam).
 
• The other names for the Godavari River are The Vriddh (Old) Ganga or the Dakshin (South) Ganga.
 
• Godavari river drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Godavari river originates from Bramhagiri mountains at Trimbakeshwar.
 
• Tributaries: Pravara, Purna, Manjira, Penganga, Wardha, Wainganga, Pranhita (combined flow of Wainganga, Penganga, Wardha), Indravati, Maner, and the Sabri.
 
• The longest tributary- The Manjira
 
• The largest tributary- The Pranhita

**Kaveri:**

 
• The Kaveri river is an Indian river flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, and the Union Territory of Puducherry.
 
• The Kaveri river rises at Talakaveri on the Brahmagiri range (Karnataka) in the Western Ghats.
 
• It is the largest river in the state of Tamil Nadu and the third largest river after Godavari and Krishna in South India.
 
• Amaravati, Bhavani, and Kabini are the tributaries of river Kaveri.
 
• The Stanley reservoir on the Kaveri river in Tamilnadu is also known as the **Mettur dam.**

**Tapi:**

 
• The Tapti (also known as the Tapi) is the second-largest west flowing river in Peninsular India and is known as ‘the twin’ or ‘the handmaid’ of the Narmada.
 
• It flows for about 724 km before outfalling into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Cambay (Gulf of Khambhat).
 
• The Tapti River along with its tributaries flows over the plains of Vidharbha, Khandesh, and Gujarat and over large areas in the state of Maharashtra and a small area in Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.
 
• Situated in the Deccan plateau, the basin is bounded by the
 
 
• Satpura range on the north,
 
• Mahadev hills on the east,
 
• Ajanta Range and the Satmala hills on the south, and
 
• by the Arabian Sea on the west.

__
 
• **On the Indian Narmada River, the Sardar Sarovar Dam (SSD) is located in the village of Kevadia in Gujarat.**

questions.question: Which of the following rivers forms the 'Dhuadhar Falls' in Madhya Pradesh?

• The falls are located near **Jabalpur**, a prominent city in the state.
 
• The name 'Dhuadhar' is derived from the Hindi words 'Dhua' meaning smoke, and 'Dhar' meaning flow, due to the mist created by the force of the water.
 
• The Narmada River is one of the major rivers in central India and is often referred to as the **'Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh'**.

• **Hydroelectric Projects:**
 
 
• Several major hydroelectric projects like the Sardar Sarovar Dam and the Indira Sagar Dam are constructed on the Narmada River.
 
• These projects are crucial for irrigation, water supply, and power generation in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is located in the western part of the country and flows through the states of **Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat. Here are some key details about the Tapi River:**
 
 
• **Origin:** The Tapi River originates in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh, near Multai town, in the Satpura Range of hills.
 
• **Course: **The river flows westward through Madhya Pradesh and enters Maharashtra near Bhusawal. It then continues its westward journey through Maharashtra, passing through cities like Jalgaon, Burhanpur, and Surat. Finally, it enters the Gulf of Khambhat in the Arabian Sea in Gujarat.

• **Sacred and Cultural Significance:** The Godavari holds immense religious importance, especially among Hindus. It is often referred to as the "Dakshina Ganga" or the Ganges of the South. 
 
• **River Basin and Irrigation:** The Godavari River has an extensive river basin covering around **312,812 square kilometers (120,777 square miles). **This vast basin provides water for irrigation, supporting agriculture and livelihoods for millions of people in the surrounding regions. 
 
• **Biodiversity and Ecosystem: **The Godavari River and its basin support rich biodiversity and a diverse ecosystem. The river sustains a variety of flora and fauna, including several endangered species.

• **Importance for Agriculture: **The Mahanadi River plays a crucial role in irrigation and agriculture in the region. Several dams and reservoirs have been constructed along its course to store water for irrigation purposes, ensuring the availability of water for crops and promoting agricultural development.
 
• **Mahanadi Delta: **The river forms a large delta known as the Mahanadi Delta, which is located in the coastal plains of Odisha. The deltaic region is rich in fertile alluvial soil, making it suitable for agriculture and supporting a diverse ecosystem.
 
• **Biodiversity and Wildlife: **The Mahanadi River and its surrounding areas are home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. The river supports rich biodiversity, including several species of fish, reptiles, and mammals. It also serves as a habitat for migratory birds, making it a significant area for birdwatching and conservation efforts.

questions.question: What is the major purpose of the Salal Dam located on Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir?

__

• It is located on the Chenab River in the Reasi district of Jammu and Kashmir, India.
 
• The dam has an installed capacity of 690 megawatts, providing significant power to the region.
 
• The construction of the Salal Dam was completed in two stages, with Stage I completed in 1987 and Stage II in 1995.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Chenab River is one of the major rivers in the Indian subcontinent, flowing through India and Pakistan.
 
• It originates from the confluence of the Chandra and Bhaga rivers in the Lahaul and Spiti districts of Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• The river is a key source of irrigation and hydroelectric power in the region.
